summary: Reusable possible-expression examples for translating astrology patterns into plain life scenarios without treating examples as predictions.
body: Use these scenarios as optional plain-language examples when repeated testimony supports a theme. They are not predictions, promises, diagnoses, or instructions. The app should phrase them as possible ways a pattern can show up.
definition: An example scenario is a plain-life illustration of how an astrological pattern may express, used only after the chart context supports the topic.
appUsage: Surface examples as 'this can look like' language, not 'this will happen' language.
Require repeated testimony before naming concrete event categories.
Keep sensitive topics broad and practical, especially health, safety, pregnancy, legal, financial, and relationship outcomes.
Use examples to clarify the life area, not to override user agency.
Do not expose source names or source files in user-facing text.
note: Distilled from approved project resources and existing knowledge-base gaps. Source files were not copied into the repository.

transitToNatal.use: Use these when a transit-to-natal contact is supported by house activation, natal promise, return chart emphasis, or repeated timing testimony.

conversationOrMessage: A text, call, email, meeting, application, result, or announcement becomes the trigger point.
A misunderstanding needs repair through direct language.
A decision becomes real once it is written, signed, sent, or said out loud.
relationshipPressure: A relationship asks for definition, boundaries, repair, or a more honest agreement.
Attraction and compatibility need to be separated instead of treated as the same thing.
The user may need to name what they want instead of waiting for the other person to guess.
careerVisibility: A role, title, client, boss, public result, or reputation issue comes into focus.
The user may be asked to lead, be seen, explain their work, or accept more responsibility.
A private effort becomes visible enough to need structure.
moneyResources: A payment, invoice, rate, debt, shared expense, purchase, or budget issue needs attention.
The user may need to price their work, ask for compensation, or stop avoiding a money conversation.
A resource pattern becomes concrete enough to plan around.
homeFamily: A home, family, moving, property, repair, caregiving, or privacy issue becomes active.
The user's emotional foundation may need practical support rather than more analysis.
A family pattern may become visible through a current logistical problem.
bodyStress: The user's body, energy, sleep, workload, or stress level asks for practical care.
A schedule or responsibility may need to be adjusted so the body is not carrying the whole cost.
If the user has a health concern, the example should direct them toward licensed support instead of interpretation.
privateClosure: A draining pattern, hidden burden, grief process, therapy theme, rest need, or private ending comes forward.
The user may need quiet, withdrawal, journaling, support, or a container for what is ending.
Closure may be the work even before the next chapter is visible.

developmentalAgeMap.use: Use these only for the optional developmental age map feature, never for current transits or exact prediction.

gestation: Inherited family conditions, prenatal atmosphere, origin stories, and the circumstances surrounding arrival.
Themes that feel older than conscious memory and may be explored symbolically rather than literally.
childhood: Home, school, caregivers, siblings, early rules, play, belonging, and the first lessons about safety.
A house period may describe the environment the child learned to adapt to, not a verdict about the child.
maturity: Partnership, work, public role, money, responsibility, family-building, and adult identity formation.
Planets in the mapped period can describe pressures, people, or events that shape the adult path.
laterLife: Legacy, simplification, mentoring, spiritual reflection, contribution, memory, and meaning beyond achievement.
Later-life themes should be presented as reflection points, not as fixed outcomes.

compositeChart.use: Use these to explain what a composite pattern can feel like inside the relationship field.

moonSaturnHard: Emotional closeness may be tied to duty, timing, distance, family responsibility, or fear of needing too much.
The bond can feel loyal but heavy unless warmth is practiced on purpose.
venusUranusHard: Affection can spark quickly and then need space just as quickly.
The relationship may need unconventional agreements, flexible timing, or honest room for independence.
marsSaturnHard: One part of the relationship pushes while another blocks, delays, critiques, or fears the consequence.
Desire, conflict, work, or momentum may need structure before it can move cleanly.
neptunePersonalHard: Idealization, rescue, secrecy, confusion, or blurred expectations can cloud what is actually happening.
The relationship needs direct questions, practical agreements, and reality checks.
plutoPersonalHard: Intensity, attachment, control, jealousy, or survival patterns may become part of the relationship climate.
Clean boundaries matter more than the magnetism.

synastry.use: Use these when close interaspects or overlays repeat a relationship theme.

twelfthHouseOverlay: The connection may work under the surface through projection, secrecy, dreams, compassion, avoidance, or unspoken emotional charge.
The user may feel the person even when the relationship is not clearly defined.
saturnContact: The Saturn person may stabilize, mentor, delay, judge, test, or structure the other person's planet.
This can support commitment, but it can also feel cold or unequal if one person becomes the authority.
venusMarsChemistry: The spark may be obvious before compatibility is proven.
Attraction can open the door, but daily emotional safety and communication decide whether the bond can live there.
nodesOrVertex: The contact may feel like a turning point, familiar pattern, or relationship that arrives with unusual timing.
Name the pull without calling it proof that the relationship must last.
fourthHouseOverlay: The planet person can touch the house person's home, family memory, privacy, and emotional roots.
This can feel deeply safe or unexpectedly exposing.
seventhHouseOverlay: The house person may experience the planet person as partner material, mirror, client, opponent, or someone who forces relationship definition.
Projection is common; the app should separate recognition from commitment.
eighthHouseOverlay: The bond may activate trust, sex, shared resources, debt, vulnerability, grief, therapy, or power dynamics.
Intensity is not enough; the relationship needs consent, clarity, and boundaries.
tenthHouseOverlay: The planet person may affect the house person's career, public role, ambition, reputation, or authority path.
Support and pressure can arrive together.

progressedLunation.use: Use these as phase examples for the progressed lunation cycle.

new: A private reset, seed, withdrawal, or new inner orientation begins before the outside life has proof.
The user may feel less visible while a new chapter gathers roots.
crescent: The new direction needs protection, repetition, and small proof.
Old habits may test whether the user will keep feeding the seed.
firstQuarter: A decision, challenge, conflict, or action point forces the new direction into motion.
The user may need to choose movement before certainty.
gibbous: Refinement, skill-building, editing, adjustment, and service to the larger aim become central.
The user may need to improve the system without turning improvement into self-attack.
full: Visibility, culmination, result, public recognition, relationship mirroring, or full awareness arrives.
The user sees what the cycle has become and what it costs to maintain.
disseminating: Teaching, sharing, distribution, mentoring, publishing, or giving the harvest away becomes important.
The question becomes who benefits from what the user has learned.
lastQuarter: Revision, release, disillusionment, restructuring, and value clarification become necessary.
The user may need to stop maintaining a form that no longer carries the meaning.
balsamic: Closure, retreat, grief, quiet preparation, spiritual practice, and behind-the-scenes completion take priority.
The next cycle is not ready to be forced yet.

chiron.use: Use these only in the optional shadow and healing layer, especially when Chiron touches a personal planet or angle.

examplesByHouse.2: Worth, money, stability, value, and the fear of never having enough.
examplesByHouse.3: Voice, learning, siblings, early school experience, and being understood.
examplesByHouse.4: Home, family, belonging, roots, privacy, and emotional safety.
examplesByHouse.5: Creativity, joy, romance, children, play, and the fear of being seen.
examplesByHouse.6: Work, usefulness, routines, body symbolism, service, and over-functioning.
examplesByHouse.7: Partnership, rejection, being chosen, projection, and healing through relationship.
examplesByHouse.8: Trust, intimacy, shared resources, grief, control, vulnerability, and deep repair.
examplesByHouse.9: Belief, meaning, faith, education, travel, and rebuilding a worldview.
examplesByHouse.10: Public role, authority, legitimacy, career, reputation, and earned confidence.
examplesByHouse.11: Belonging, friendship, groups, community, exclusion, and making room for outsiders.
examplesByHouse.12: Hidden wounds, inherited sorrow, solitude, spiritual sensitivity, and what needs a safe container.

prohibitions: Do not treat examples as predictions.
Do not use examples to diagnose medical, mental health, legal, financial, or safety outcomes.
Do not include source names, source titles, or copied source text.
Do not surface exact developmental age tables or proprietary formulas.
Do not make past-life framing mandatory or literal.
weighting: Use examples only after the main interpretation is grounded.
For timing, require repeated testimony before examples become concrete.
For relationships, separate attraction, compatibility, durability, and health.
For body-related topics, keep examples symbolic and direct users to licensed support when needed.
For optional lenses, label the lens clearly before showing examples.
